headline: High-risk filesystem and workflow overlap: ECC can write and modify git state while plano has broad egress, creating medium prompt-injection, leakage, and cascading-error risks.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: ECC can read/write the filesystem, use MCP, and exposes shared files like ~/.claude and ~/.cursor/ecc; plano consumes an OpenAI-compatible chat endpoint and has broad egress. That creates a plausible content-to-instructions bridge if plano outputs are copied into ECC or shared files, though no direct shared channel is documented.
conditions: IF plano outputs are copied into ECC-managed files or MCP inputs
IF both agents are pointed at the same workspace or config directory
mitigations: Separate the agents into distinct workspaces
Disable MCP ingestion for untrusted plano outputs
Require manual review before pasting plano text into ECC
Use read-only mounts for shared reference files
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging between agents

B_data_leakage.rationale: ECC touches security findings, git history, documentation, and multiple local config paths, while plano sends requests to an OpenAI-compatible endpoint over broad egress. If they share a workspace or credentials, ECC-held sensitive material could flow into plano's remote context, but the profiles do not prove a default shared directory.
conditions: IF ECC and plano share files containing secrets or findings
IF plano is configured to include local file contents in remote prompts
mitigations: Keep secrets out of any shared directory
Restrict plano to non-sensitive inputs only
Rotate credentials before testing cross-agent workflows
Audit outbound requests for file-content leakage
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent data boundaries

C_capability_conflict.rationale: ECC has write_filesystem, modify_git_state, and spawn_subprocesses; plano has broad network egress and an out-of-process dataplane but no write or git capability is shown. The main conflict is on shared mutable resources if both are aimed at the same repo or config tree; uncertainty keeps this at medium rather than low.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same git repository
IF plano writes configuration while ECC edits the same files
mitigations: Assign separate repos or branches
Serialize edits with a lock file
Have one agent operate read-only
Review git diffs before merge
requires-engineering: add optimistic concurrency controls

D_cascading_error.rationale: ECC can generate and modify code, docs, and security findings, while plano is a routing/gateway-style agent that may forward or act on upstream text. If plano treats ECC output as authoritative without verification, errors can cascade into downstream actions; the profiles do not show a built-in verification step.
conditions: IF plano consumes ECC-produced text as trusted input
IF ECC output is used to drive downstream API calls or routing decisions
mitigations: Insert a human review step
Require schema validation on ECC outputs
Limit ECC to draft-only mode
Log and compare source citations before action
requires-engineering: add verification gates in plano

E_compliance.rationale: ECC explicitly handles session retention, hooks, and security findings, while plano only lists logs, traces, and metrics with no stated residency or retention mismatch. The profiles do not document a concrete compliance conflict, so this is limited to a low, documentation-gap risk rather than a proven breach.
conditions: IF the same regulated data class is stored in both agents
IF retention or residency policies differ in deployment
mitigations: Document data-class handling for both agents
Set explicit retention limits
Avoid placing regulated data in plano logs
Review residency requirements before deployment
requires-engineering: align compliance policies across systems
